verified_authorities.case_name: Secretary for Justice v Lam Tat Ming and Another
verified_authorities.exact_quote: as soon as a law enforcement officer has evidence which would afford reasonable grounds for suspecting that a person has committed an offence, he shall caution the suspect before putting any or any further questions to him
verified_authorities.principle_summary: A suspect's right of silence is protected by the Secretary for Security rules and directions; once there are reasonable grounds to suspect an offence, caution is required before questioning.

verified_authorities.case_name: Secretary for Justice v Lam Tat Ming and Another
verified_authorities.exact_quote: once the officer actively questions the suspect, we enter into an area which may engage the exercise of the residual discretion
verified_authorities.principle_summary: Active questioning by an undercover officer that procures a confession may engage the court's residual discretion because the suspect could not be cautioned.

verified_authorities.case_name: Secretary for Justice v Lam Tat Ming and Another
verified_authorities.exact_quote: If however what the officer does amounts to interrogation, the discretion would ordinarily be exercised so as to exclude the confession
verified_authorities.principle_summary: If undercover conduct amounts to interrogation, the residual discretion would ordinarily exclude the confession because it derogates from the accused's right of silence and prejudices a fair trial.

verified_authorities.case_name: Leung Kwok Hung and Others v HKSAR
